propositions: The `[operator-attested]` evidence contract requires provenance of the attestation event (change id / vote / timestamp) but not provenance of the measurement itself (environment, principal, privilege level), creating an escape hatch where measurements taken in wrong environments or under excessive privilege are recorded as settled fact.

Two specific escapes occurred: (1) bedrock measurements from account 579718921998 / us-east-2 recorded as valid for account 896586841071 / us-east-1, and (2) live bedrock:Converse calls under bedrock:* privilege offered as validation for a scoped bedrock:InvokeModel grant that would have failed in production.

The fix extends the attestation contract with four required fields (environment, principal, privilege_posture, instrument) declared on an indented continuation line under the [operator-attested] checkbox, pinned by deterministic syntax validation with no LLM involvement.

A new deterministic check (det_measurement_provenance.py) validates presence and shape of the four provenance fields (non-placeholder values, enum membership for privilege_posture and instrument literals) as a pure text/structure validation, leaving semantic contradictions to an AGENT-tier criterion.

An AGENT-tier criterion (project.measurement-provenance) reads the declared environment against repo facts (e.g., Terraform backend account in infra/terraform/versions.tf), checks privilege_posture against criterion scope, and validates instrument type against authorization claims, with no world measurements re-run.
